notes.text: The undergraduate curriculum leads to the Bachelor of Science with a major in Occupational Therapy. Incoming freshmen may apply to the bachelor’s to doctorate program in occupational therapy. The program is part of an accelerated Bachelor’s to Doctorate (BS-OTD) pathway that integrates undergraduate and graduate coursework. Eligible USC freshmen and sophomores may apply to change their major to the program. Students majoring in occupational therapy begin full-time graduate study during their senior year, , which helps reduce overall time and cost of education and prepares them earlier for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy® (NBCOT) examination. Successful completion of an Occupational Therapy Doctorate (OTD) degree, including successful completion of a minimum of 24 full-time weeks of clinical fieldwork, qualifies students for eligibility to sit for the NBCOT examination. Certification from the board and state licensure are required to practice as an occupational therapist.

sections.title: Admission Criteria for Current USC Students (Major Change)

notes.text: Current USC freshmen and sophomores may apply to change their major to the Occupational Therapy (BS-OTD) program. Applicants must have a minimum USC GPA of 3.0 (or a 3.0 high school GPA if enrolled at USC for less than one semester). Applicants must submit a personal statement, develop an academic plan with the OT Major Adviser, and submit materials to the Chan Division admissions office.

notes.text: The university’s general education (GE) program provides a coherent, integrated introduction to the breadth of knowledge you will need to become a generally well-educated person. This program is effective for all students entering USC in fall 2015 or later, or transfer students beginning college elsewhere at that time and subsequently transferring to USC. The general education program requires eight courses in six Core Literacies, plus two courses in Global Perspectives (which may double-count with courses in the Core Literacies) and two courses in writing. See General Education for more information.

notes.text: Undergraduate occupational therapy students must maintain a GPA of at least 3.0 (A = 4.0) in all required OT courses in order to continue into the graduate program. If an undergraduate student’s OT grade point average (GPA) falls below 3.0, or if the cumulative undergraduate GPA falls below 3.0 at the end of the fall semester of the senior year, continuance is not assured.
